questions.question: Define electric potential and electric potential difference. Write their SI units.
questions.solution:
**Electric potential:** The electric potential at a point in an electric field is the amount of work done in bringing a **unit positive charge** from infinity to that point without acceleration.
$$V = \frac{W}{q}\qquad \text{SI unit: volt (V, J C}^{-1}\text{)}$$
It is a **scalar** quantity.

**Electric potential difference:** The potential difference between two points $A$ and $B$ is the work done in taking a unit positive charge from $A$ to $B$.
$$V_{AB} = V_B - V_A = \frac{W_{AB}}{q}$$

Equipotential surfaces have the **same** potential. Potential is zero at infinity and is **always** positive for a positive charge.
questions.knowledgeNote: Electric potential is work done per unit positive charge brought from infinity, measured in volts.
